adult_dose: 500-1000 mg BD with food (start 500 mg, escalate based on HbA1c)
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Lifestyle modification must accompany. HbA1c target ≤7.0%
contraindications: eGFR <30; IV contrast; acute illness; hepatic failure

adult_dose: Metformin 500-1000 mg BD + Glimepiride 1-2 mg OD BBF (or Gliclazide 60 mg MR OD BBF)
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Dual therapy when monotherapy fails. Monitor for hypoglycemia with SU.

adult_dose: Metformin 500-1000 mg BD + Sitagliptin 100 mg OD (or Vildagliptin 50 mg BD or Linagliptin 5 mg OD)
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Weight neutral. Linagliptin has no dose adjustment in renal failure.

adult_dose: Metformin 500-1000 mg BD + Dapagliflozin 10 mg OD
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Cardioprotective and renoprotective. Maintain genital hygiene. Adequate hydration.
contraindications: eGFR <45; recurrent UTI/genital infections; DKA risk

adult_dose: Metformin + GLP-1 RA as per drug-specific dosing
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Weight reducing. Preferred if BMI >30 or obesity.

adult_dose: Basal insulin 0.1-0.2 units/kg OD at bedtime; titrate by 2 units every 3 days to FPG 80-130
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Titrate dose every 3 days. Start with 10 units if no weight-based calculation available.

adult_dose: 1.6-1.8 mcg/kg/day OD fasting; no food for 1 hr after
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Take 30-45 min before breakfast. Separate from calcium/iron/antacids by 4 hrs. Target TSH 1-2.5 mU/L (young); 1.5-3 (middle-aged); higher targets in elderly.
contraindications: Untreated adrenal insufficiency (central hypothyroidism – treat adrenal first)

adult_dose: Start 12.5-25 mcg/day; increase by 12.5-25 mcg every 3-4 weeks until target TSH
line_of_treatment: First line – Elderly patients or known CAD
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Elderly TSH targets: <60 yrs >4.5; 60-70 yrs >6.0; 70-80 yrs >7.0-8.0 mU/L. Avoid rapid correction in elderly.
contraindications: IHD – aggressive replacement may precipitate angina

adult_dose: Start 25-50 mcg OD; titrate to TSH
line_of_treatment: Conditional – treat if TSH >10 or presence of symptoms
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Consider treating subclinical hypothyroidism if: large goitre / positive TPO antibody / ASCVD / heart failure / dyslipidemia / infertility / depression / refractory anaemia.

pediatric_dose: 10-15 mcg/kg/day OD (given with breast milk in powdered form)
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Follow up at 2 and 4 weeks; every 1-2 months in first 6 months; every 3-4 months from 6 months to 3 yrs. Target FT4: 1.4-2.3 ng/dl; TSH: 0.5-2 mU/L.

adult_dose: 100 mg BD
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Empirical treatment – no tests needed for simple cystitis in females. Take with food.
contraindications: eGFR <45; near-term pregnancy; avoid urine alkaliniser concurrently

adult_dose: 1 DS tab BD
line_of_treatment: First line – Alternative (if local sensitivity allows)
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Check local resistance patterns. Avoid in 1st trimester and near term pregnancy.
contraindications: G6PD deficiency; sulfa allergy; 1st trimester/near-term pregnancy

adult_dose: 100 mg BD
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Males require 7 days (not 3 days). All other male UTI (pyelonephritis, prostatitis) must be referred.

adult_dose: 500 mg BD
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Alternative to nitrofurantoin in males.

adult_dose: 500 mg BD
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Consider initial parenteral dose: Ceftriaxone 1-2 g IV/IM x1 or Gentamicin 5 mg/kg IM x1 before starting oral.

adult_dose: 750 mg OD
notes: Source: ICMR STW. 5-day course with 750 mg equivalent to 7-day 500 mg course.

adult_dose: 500 mg BD
notes: Source: ICMR STW. 10-14 day course required for pyelonephritis.

adult_dose: 100 mg BD
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Check urine culture at 1st antenatal visit. Avoid near term (week 36+). Repeat urine C/S 7 days after Rx.

adult_dose: 500 mg QID
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Safe in pregnancy. If recurrent UTI in pregnancy: antibiotic prophylaxis till term.

adult_dose: 1 DS tab BD (older >35 yrs)
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Treat for 6 weeks. Digital rectal exam: tender prostate. Image to rule out abscess.

adult_dose: Doxycycline 100 mg BD x 6 weeks + Ceftriaxone 250 mg IM single dose (for gonorrhoea cover)
line_of_treatment: First line – Prostatitis young males (chlamydia/gonorrhoea cover)
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Young males: STI-associated prostatitis. Cover chlamydia (doxy/azithro) + gonorrhoea (ceftriaxone IM).

adult_dose: 50 mg OD at HS or post-coital
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Post-coital voiding also advised. Estrogen vaginal cream for post-menopausal recurrent UTI.

adult_dose: 10 ml TDS in water
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Relieves dysuria by alkalinising urine. Avoid if on nitrofurantoin (nitrofurantoin requires acidic urine).

adult_dose: 200 mg TDS x 2 days
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Turns urine orange – warn patient. Use only for 2 days.

adult_dose: 20-80 mg OD PO; IV 10-80 mg SOS in acute stage; change to oral when symptoms subside
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Start with IV in acute/admitted patients; switch to oral once decongested. Monitor serum electrolytes, creatinine and uric acid.

adult_dose: 50-200 mg BD; start with low dose if BP >100 mmHg, normal electrolytes, creatinine <2.5 mg/dl; uptitrate 1-2 weekly
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Uptitrate every 1-2 weeks to maximum tolerable dose. Monitor BP and electrolytes before every increment.
contraindications: Pregnancy; bilateral renal artery stenosis; concurrent ACE inhibitor (36 hr washout needed); creatinine >2.5 mg/dl

adult_dose: 3.125-25 mg BD; start after decongestion with low dose (BP >100 mmHg, HR >60/min); uptitrate 1-2 weekly
line_of_treatment: First line – Beta blocker for HFrEF
notes: Source: ICMR STW. START ONLY AFTER DECONGESTION. Never initiate in acute decompensation. Monitor BP, HR, and watch for worsening CHF symptoms.
contraindications: Acute decompensation; HR <60; BP <100; Asthma/COPD (use bisoprolol instead)

adult_dose: 12.5-50 mg BD; start after decongestion
line_of_treatment: First line – Beta blocker for HFrEF alternative
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Alternative to carvedilol. Start after decongestion only.

adult_dose: 1.25-10 mg OD; start after decongestion
line_of_treatment: First line – Beta blocker (preferred in COPD/asthma over carvedilol)
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Once-daily dosing advantage. Preferred if asthma/COPD (more cardioselective).

adult_dose: 25-50 mg OD
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Monitor serum potassium and creatinine every 2-4 weeks. Stop if K+ >5.5 mEq/L or creatinine >2.5 mg/dl.

adult_dose: Dapagliflozin 10 mg OD or Empagliflozin 10 mg OD
line_of_treatment: First line – add-on (HFrEF and HFpEF, diabetic or non-diabetic)
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Now recommended in heart failure regardless of diabetes status. Reduces hospitalisation.

adult_dose: 20-80 mg IV bolus; repeat every 6-8 hrs as needed
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Give IV in acute decompensation. O2 if SpO2 <90%. Monitor urine output, electrolytes, creatinine daily.

adult_dose: Apply LA BD
notes: Source: ICMR STW. ALWAYS treat till all lesions completely resolved. Treat for at least 3-8 weeks. Do NOT stop on partial improvement. DO NOT use steroid-containing creams.

adult_dose: Apply LA BD
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Safer option in pregnancy. Maximum safety data for miconazole and clotrimazole in pregnancy.

adult_dose: Apply LA BD
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Fungicidal (not just static). Shorter treatment course.

adult_dose: Apply LA BD
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Also useful for seborrhoeic dermatitis when used as shampoo.

condition_aliases: Extensive Tinea;Widespread Ring Worm;Tinea Corporis Extensive
adult_dose: 250 mg BD
notes: Source: ICMR STW. TREAT TILL ALL LESIONS COMPLETELY RESOLVED. Follow up every 2 weeks. Never stop on partial improvement.
contraindications: Hepatic disease; monitor LFT if >4 weeks

adult_dose: 100-200 mg OD (with food)
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Take with food for absorption. Monitor LFT. Refer if no improvement after 4 weeks.
contraindications: Hepatic disease; heart failure; multiple drug interactions

adult_dose: 50-150 mg OD
line_of_treatment: First line – Systemic alternative (also preferred in pregnancy if systemic required)
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Weekly fluconazole 150 mg also used for tinea. Preferred if systemic antifungal needed in pregnancy.

adult_dose: 500 mg BD
line_of_treatment: Alternative systemic (older drug, less preferred now)
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Older drug. Requires prolonged treatment. Take with fatty food.

adult_dose: Cetirizine 10 mg HS or Levocetirizine 5 mg OD HS
notes: Source: ICMR STW. For symptomatic itch relief only. Does not treat fungal infection.

adult_dose: 250 mg BD
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Inform patient: normal nail takes several months to appear after treatment completion. Monitor LFT.

adult_dose: 200 mg BD x 7 days/month (2 pulses for fingernails; 3 pulses for toenails) OR 100 mg BD x 12 weeks continuous
line_of_treatment: First line – Onychomycosis alternative (pulse preferred for toenails)
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Pulse therapy: 200 mg BD for 7 days, repeat monthly. Monitor LFT.

adult_dose: Apply to affected nail once weekly
line_of_treatment: Topical – Limited nail disease (<50% nail surface, not reaching lunula)
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Also for patients with contraindications to oral antifungals. Keep separate nail clippers. Avoid pedicure/manicure.

adult_dose: Apply LA OD
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Also for tertiary care use. Prolonged treatment required for palms/soles.

condition_aliases: Scabies;Intense Itching at Night;Interdigital Itch;Mite Infestation
adult_dose: Apply whole body from neck downwards on dry clean skin; leave 8-12 hrs (overnight); wash off. 30 g per adult application. Repeat after 7-14 days.
pediatric_dose: Same as adult. In infants: also treat face and scalp. 15 g for children <5 yrs.
notes: Source: ICMR STW. TREAT ENTIRE SKIN, NOT LESIONS ALONE. TREAT ALL FAMILY MEMBERS AND CLOSE CONTACTS SIMULTANEOUSLY. Special attention to interdigital webspaces, axillae, wrists, genitalia, buttocks. Re-apply if hands washed within 8 hrs.

adult_dose: 200 mcg/kg (up to 12 mg); 2 doses 1 week apart; taken with food
line_of_treatment: Oral alternative – poor compliance with topical / severe disease
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Use when compliance with topical is poor. Take with food for absorption. TREAT ALL CONTACTS simultaneously.
contraindications: Infants; children <5 yrs or <15 kg; pregnancy – use permethrin in these groups

adult_dose: Levocetirizine 5 mg OD HS or Cetirizine 10 mg HS
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Itching can continue for several weeks after successful treatment – reassure patient and continue antihistamines. Repeated applications NOT required for persistent itch.

adult_dose: Apply whole body from neck down; leave 8-12 hrs; wash off
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Alternative to permethrin. AVOID in infants – neurotoxic risk in young children.
contraindications: Infants; children <2 yrs; pregnancy; seizure disorders

adult_dose: Ivermectin on days 1, 2, 8, 9, 15 (+ days 22, 29 in severe cases) PLUS Permethrin 5% cream daily x 7 days then twice weekly until cure
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Keratolytic (Salicylic acid 3-6%) may be used over crusts to enhance penetration.
contraindications: Pregnancy; <15 kg (for ivermectin – use permethrin only)

adult_dose: Clobetasol propionate potent topical steroid LA OR Triamcinolone acetonide 10 mg/mL intralesional injection
line_of_treatment: For persistent nodular lesions after scabies treatment
notes: Source: ICMR STW. For persistent nodules on male genitalia or other sites after successful scabies eradication. NOT for active scabies treatment.
contraindications: Active infection; skin atrophy risk with prolonged use

adult_dose: HbA1c every 6-12 months (3-monthly if uncontrolled). Annual: ECG, urine ACR, dilated fundoscopy, foot examination.
notes: Source: ICMR STW. Metabolic targets: HbA1c ≤7%; FPG 80-130 mg/dl; PPBG <180 mg/dl; BP 140/90 (<130/80 in CKD); LDL <100 mg/dl (<70 in CAD).

adult_dose: Wash clothes, towels, bed linen used in preceding 3 days in hot water; dry in sun. Items that cannot be washed: seal in plastic bag for at least 3 days (useful for shoes and non-washable items).
notes: Source: ICMR STW. All family members MUST be treated simultaneously. If itching >3-4 weeks or new lesions appear, suspect reinfestation (all contacts not treated simultaneously).
